title: Built-in web_search tool missing from the built-in tools list
skill_evidence: references/custom-tools.md:127-138 - built-in list (roll_dice ... update_about_me, spotify_*) has no web_search; it appears only in the reserved-names line :280. :127 also says '~18-tool flat list'
reality: packages/shared/src/features/function-calls/tool-registry.generated.ts:25-45 BUILT_IN_TOOLS = 19 definitions incl. web_search (tools/web-search/manifest.ts: query required, limit 1-8, default 5). tool-executor.ts:889-905 runs it against https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/ (10s timeout, https only). It is not in DEFAULT_OFF_TOOL_NAMES (services/generation/tool-resolution-runtime.ts:166), so a chat with Enable Tool Use on and no tools added gets it automatically. Added v2.0.7 (#3074). Spotify nuance: the six spotify_* definitions also ship in the base Engine (same registry; names reserved for custom tools at custom-tools.routes.ts:18-20) and are default-off; they are only offered when a Music DJ agent has Spotify connected with user-modify-playback-state scope (tool-resolution-runtime.ts:937-955, spotify/spotify.service.ts:241-256)
fix: custom-tools.md Built-In Tools: add a bullet '`web_search` - compact public web results (title, URL, snippet) via DuckDuckGo Lite; `query` + optional `limit` 1-8 (default 5); no setup, on by default when Enable Tool Use is on with no tool filter (v2.0.7, #3074) - check this before suggesting a search webhook.' Change '~18-tool' to '19 built-in definitions'. Reword the Spotify line: the definitions ship in the Engine and their names stay reserved, but they're default-off and only offered once the Music DJ agent has Spotify connected.

title: Agent-only built-in tools never reach the main chat model
skill_evidence: references/custom-tools.md:127 and :133-136 list save_lorebook_entry, edit_chat_message, read_/append_chat_summary, read_/write_chat_variable as built-ins that 'work the same way'; :265 'With it on and no tools added below, a chat can use *all* globally enabled tools'
reality: services/generation/tool-resolution-runtime.ts:151-158 AGENT_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES = save_lorebook_entry, read_chat_summary, append_chat_summary, read_chat_variable, write_chat_variable, edit_chat_message; isChatToolResolved (:205-212) returns false for them, so they are dropped from chat turns even when added under Function Calling. The Chat Settings picker still lists every BUILT_IN_TOOL (client/src/components/chat/ChatSettingsDrawer.tsx:2526-2532), so adding them looks like it works. DEFAULT_OFF_TOOL_NAMES (:166) = update_about_me + the spotify_* tools: they are left out of the 'no filter = everything' default and must be added explicitly
fix: custom-tools.md Built-In Tools: mark the six as 'agent-only: offered only to agents that list them in enabledTools (Agent editor -> Tools / Function Calling), never to the main chat model even if added in Chat Settings -> Function Calling'. In the UI-naming paragraph (:265) replace 'all globally enabled tools' with 'every enabled custom tool plus the chat-eligible built-ins; agent-only tools are never sent, and update_about_me / spotify_* stay off until added explicitly'.

title: Hidden chat context payload is much larger than described
skill_evidence: references/custom-tools.md:294 'chat mode, active persona name, character names, saved chat variables and, in Game Mode, the game state'; :18 and assets/custom-tool-webhook.template.md:50 mention 'a context object' with no shape
reality: services/generation/tool-resolution-runtime.ts:311-403 buildCustomToolHiddenContext returns {chatId, chatMode, personaId, personaName, characterId, characterName, characterIds, characterNames, characters[{id,name}], variables (chat agentVariables), macros{chatId, chatMode, personaId, user, userName, persona (persona description+personality+backstory+appearance+scenario), characterId, characterName, char, charName, characters, description, personality, backstory, appearance, scenario, example (example dialogue), charSysInfo (card system prompt), charPostHistory (post-history instructions), input (last user message text), date, time, datetime, isotime, weekday}, recentMessages[{id, role, characterId}], gameState}. Webhooks get it as body.context and scripts as `context` (tool-executor.ts:446-449, custom-tool-script.worker.ts:18). Even the editor help text (en.json ui.agents.tooleditor.variableIncludesChatIdModePersonaCharacterIdsNames) understates it
fix: custom-tools.md includeHiddenContext section: list the real top-level keys and say plainly that `macros` carries the primary character's full card text (incl. system prompt and post-history instructions), the persona's card fields and the user's last message, so turning it on for a third-party webhook sends card and persona text off-box. Add the key list (or a one-line pointer) next to the request shape in assets/custom-tool-webhook.template.md section 3.

title: Regex trimStrings removes text from the whole result, not just the match
skill_evidence: references/custom-tools.md:333 '`trimStrings` | Strings stripped from the match'
reality: server/src/services/regex/regex-application.ts:176-180 and client/src/hooks/use-apply-regex.ts:150-154: after the replacement runs, each trim string is removed with split/join from the entire resulting text. That happens everywhere in the message, even when the regex matched nothing. en.json ui.agents.regexscripteditor.additionalStringsToRemoveFromTheResultAfterThe: 'Additional strings to remove from the result after the regex replacement.'
fix: custom-tools.md regex Fields table: '`trimStrings` | Strings deleted from the whole text after the replacement runs (every occurrence, whether or not the pattern matched). Keep them specific.'

title: Wound-track combat health requires combat.damageKinds
skill_evidence: references/rulesets.md:62 says only that '`combat.damageKinds` on a pool-health ruleset is refused, not ignored'
reality: packages/shared/src/schemas/ruleset.schema.ts:4897-4905: when combat.health names a wound track, damageKinds is required ('Health is the wound track ..., so the block says what kind of harm its damage is'). Shape at :2425-2427 is {default: <kind id>, byType?: {<damage type>: <kind id>}, marks: 'per-blow'|'per-point'} with no default for marks, and default/byType values must be kinds of that track (:4907-4925). This is the reverse of the pool refusal at :4928-4935
fix: rulesets.md Health pool vs. wound track bullet: add 'and the reverse - a wound-track `combat.health` must declare `combat.damageKinds` {default, byType?, marks: per-blow|per-point}, or the file is refused'.

title: Custom tool dispatch no longer goes through the executor switch's default case
skill_evidence: references/custom-tools.md:140 'Custom tools run through the same executor - they just hit the `default` case in the switch that tries the custom tools list.'
reality: server/src/services/tools/tool-executor.ts:244-281 executeToolCalls resolves the built-in validator first, then the custom tool list, then package (capability) tools, and validates arguments before each. executeBuiltInTool's default case (:360-365) only returns {error:'Unknown tool'}
fix: custom-tools.md:140: 'Custom tools run through the same executor: a call resolves built-in -> custom -> package tool, with arguments validated against the tool's schema first (tool-executor.ts executeToolCalls).' This also lines up with the 'built-in -> custom -> package' sentence at :149.

title: Schema comments claim webhookUrl/staticResult/scriptBody are 'required'
skill_evidence: references/custom-tools.md:15-17 '// required if executionType is "webhook"/"static"/"script"' vs :40 'Returns `{ result: tool.staticResult ?? "OK", ... }`'
reality: packages/shared/src/schemas/custom-tool.schema.ts:17-19: all three are nullable().default(null), with no cross-field check, and ToolEditor.tsx:200-202 saves null when the field is empty. At call time (tool-executor.ts): static with no result returns 'OK' (:437), webhook with no URL returns {error:'No webhook URL configured'} (:440), script with no body returns {error:'No script body configured'} (:487)
fix: custom-tools.md schema block: change the three comments to 'used when executionType is X (not enforced at save; static falls back to "OK", a missing URL/body fails at call time)'.

title: Tool argument validation and parameter-schema constraints undocumented
skill_evidence: references/custom-tools.md:101-123 (Parameters Schema) and :259 'A tool imported from a hand-edited file with a broken parameter schema is silently skipped'
reality: tool-executor.ts:258-263 + tools/tool-arguments-validator.ts: the model's arguments are Ajv-validated against parametersSchema before the webhook/script runs. Failure returns {error:'Invalid arguments for <name>: ...'} to the model, and enum failures name the allowed values. tool-resolution-runtime.ts:405-470 validateToolSchema: root type must be 'object' (filled in if absent), each property `type` must be ONE string of string/number/integer/boolean/array/object/null (a type array like ["string","null"] is refused), and enum/required must be arrays. Any enabled tool that fails is skipped with only a server-log warning (:599-608), whether it was imported or built in the editor
fix: custom-tools.md Parameters Schema: add 'Arguments are validated against this schema before your webhook/script runs, and a mismatch goes back to the model as an error. Keep `type` a single string (no type arrays). A schema the engine can't accept makes the tool silently disappear from chats (server log only), whether imported or hand-built.' Widen :259 the same way.

title: ReDoS-flagged regex is skipped on display too, not only prompt-side
skill_evidence: references/custom-tools.md:320 'prompt-side application still skips a pattern that fails the check'
reality: server/src/services/regex/regex-application.ts:169 (prompt) and client/src/hooks/use-apply-regex.ts:145 (display) both run `if (!isPatternSafe(findRegex)) continue;`, so a flagged script that was kept on import does nothing on either surface
fix: custom-tools.md:320: 'but application (display and prompt) skips a pattern that fails the check, so the kept script does nothing until rewritten.'

title: Full page access acknowledgement is route-enforced, not a schema literal
skill_evidence: references/extensions.md:241-244 '`acknowledgeFullPageAccess: z.literal(true)` - additionally required... Because both are `z.literal(true)`, neither can be defaulted or skipped'
reality: packages/shared/src/schemas/personal-extension.schema.ts:96 `acknowledgeFullPageAccess: z.literal(true).optional()`. The requirement is enforced in server/src/routes/personal-extensions.routes.ts:1287-1289 (HTTP 400 'Full page access must be explicitly acknowledged.'). Only acknowledgeSandboxedCode is a required literal (:95)
fix: extensions.md approval bullets: 'acknowledgeFullPageAccess is an optional literal(true) in the schema, and the approve route refuses (400) a Full page access package without it'. Keep the conclusion that it can't be skipped.
